description:
A Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life
by Acharya Shantideva | Taught by Venerable Gyalten Lekden
Sunday Morning Teachings

Composed in 8th-century India by the monk-poet Acharya Shantideva, A Guide to the Bodhisattva's Way of Life(Bodhicharyavatara) is one of the most beloved texts in the entire Mahayana Buddhist tradition. Written in exquisite verse, it is at once a philosophical treatise and a deeply personal outpouring of aspiration — tracing the bodhisattva's path from the very arising of bodhichitta, the wish to attain enlightenment for the sake of all beings, through the six perfections of generosity, ethics, patience, joyous effort, concentration, and wisdom. Its chapter on patience and its closing chapter on wisdom, in particular, have shaped Buddhist thought and practice for over a millennium, and the text remains a touchstone for practitioners across every school of Tibetan Buddhism.

Under the guidance of Venerable Gyalten Lekden, these Sunday morning sessions offer a chance to sit with Shantideva's verses slowly and carefully — unpacking their meaning and, more importantly, exploring how this ancient poetry of compassion can transform the way we meet our own everyday struggles, relationships, and aspirations. It is both a study of philosophy and a training of the heart.

All are warmly welcome to join, whether encountering this text for the first time or returning to it as an old friend.

description:
Middle Length Lamrim
by Je Tsongkhapa | Taught by Venerable Gyalten Lekden
Saturday Evening Teachings

The Middle Length Lamrim (Lam-rim chen-mo 'bring) is one of the great masterworks of Tibetan Buddhism, composed by Je Tsongkhapa (1357–1419), the founder of the Gelug tradition. Written as a more compact companion to his monumental Great Treatise on the Stages of the Path, it distills centuries of Indian and Tibetan wisdom into a clear, practical roadmap — the "stages of the path" (lam-rim) that lead a practitioner from the very first steps of Dharma practice all the way to full enlightenment. Drawing on the lineage of Atisha's Lamp for the Path, Tsongkhapa's text weaves together sutra and tantra, philosophy and meditation, into a single unified structure that generations of practitioners have relied on ever since.

Each Saturday evening, this rich text comes alive under the guidance of Venerable Gyalten Lekden, whose warm and thorough teaching style makes the profound accessible — grounding ancient philosophy in the practicalities of everyday life and meditation practice. Students are led step by step through the path, building both understanding and the motivation to put it into practice.

Whether you are new to the Lamrim or returning to deepen your study, all are warmly welcome to join.
